title: Separated locally quasi-finite scheme descent is effective for a singleton fpqc cover
statement: Let $f:T\prime\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] such that $\{f\}$ is an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Let $V\to T\prime$ be a separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite] morphism of schemes. Suppose $V$ is equipped with a descent datum over $T\prime/T$ [def-pd-descent-datum]: writing $p_0,p_1:T\prime\times_TT\prime\to T\prime$ [def-pc-fibre-product], it is an isomorphism $\phi:p_0^*V\xrightarrow{\sim}p_1^*V$ with $p_{02}^*\phi=p_{12}^*\phi\circ p_{01}^*\phi$ on the triple fibre product. Then there exist a $T$-scheme $W$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:W\times_TT\prime\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ over $T\prime$ which identifies the canonical descent datum of $W\times_TT\prime$ with $\phi$. No quasi-compactness, finite presentation, or separatedness hypothesis on $T$ or $T\prime$ is imposed, and $V\to T\prime$ need not be quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 0APK, lemma-ind-quasi-affine, specialized to a singleton fpqc covering and combined with More on Morphisms Tag 0AP9, lemma-etale-separated-ind-quasi-affine (more-morphisms.tex: a separated locally quasi-finite morphism is ind-quasi-affine).

proof.text: Let $U\subseteq T\prime$ be an affine open, let $V_U\subseteq V$ be its inverse image (the open subscheme representing $V\times_{T\prime}U$ [def-pc-fibre-product]), let $K\subseteq V_U$ be a quasi-compact open subscheme, and let $h:K\to U$ be the restricted morphism. (a) $h$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]: since $U\to T\prime$ is an open immersion, $K\times_UK=K\times_{T\prime}K$ is the open subscheme of $V\times_{T\prime}V$ over $K\times K$, and the diagonal of $V\to T\prime$, a closed immersion, has inverse image $K$ over it; the restriction of a closed immersion over an open of its target is a closed immersion, and it is the diagonal of $h$. (b) $h$ is locally quasi-finite by [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-restriction-to-opens] applied to $V\to T\prime$, the open $K$ and the open $U$. (c) $h$ is quasi-compact: $K$ is quasi-compact and $U$ is affine, hence quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) applies. (d) $h$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-locally-finite-type] and (b). By [lemma-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism-of-quasi-finite], whose four hypotheses are (a)–(d), $h:K\to U$ is quasi-affine [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism]. Thus $V\to T\prime$ has the property required in [lem-a1-ind-quasi-affine-fpqc-effective-descent]: for every affine open of $T\prime$, every quasi-compact open of its inverse image is quasi-affine over it.

source.place: Tag 0AP9, lemma-etale-separated-ind-quasi-affine, proof: $U\to V$ is separated quasi-finite, then Zariski's Main Theorem in the form Tag 02LR, lemma-quasi-finite-separated-quasi-affine

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-ind-quasi-affine-fpqc-effective-descent] to the singleton fpqc covering $f$ and the given descent datum. Its hypotheses are exactly the covering condition, the quasi-affine quasi-compact-open property from step 1, and the stated cocycle. It yields a $T$-scheme $W$ and an isomorphism $W\times_TT\prime\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ over $T\prime$ inducing the given datum, with no quasi-compactness or finite-presentation assumption on $V\to T\prime$.
